items.title: Euro FX futures decline as a stronger U.S. dollar snaps a 2-day rally.
items.excerpt: Euro FX futures slide to start the week as a firming U.S. dollar snaps a two-day rally, pushing the euro back toward 1.12. Euro volatility rises alongside the pullback toward 18-month lows, while speculators expand their net short positions to the highest level in 10 years.

items.title: Tech rebounds as AI earnings kick off.
items.excerpt: Bob Iaccino of Path Trading Partners breaks down the morning's market action as tech stocks lead a rebound across U.S. equities. He analyzes the slight downward shift in market expectations for Federal Reserve rate hikes in October and December. With a major earnings week kicking off, Iaccino explores how upcoming reports from Meta, Tesla, and Netflix could impact the tech sector and whether investor appetite for AI spending remains strong. Plus, a look at the slide in crude oil prices following an easing of sanctions on Russia, and a preview of crucial economic data ahead, including the PBoC rate decision and U.S. housing figures.

items.title: Euro futures hit 17-month low as U.S. inflation tops expectations.
items.excerpt: Euro futures drop to a 17-month low as a divergence in U.S. and European inflation data reshapes interest rate expectations. Bob Iaccino unpacks the market reaction after U.S. core inflation rose 2.6%, keeping the possibility of a late-October Fed rate hike in the conversation. Meanwhile, German inflation held steady at 3.3%, reinforcing market expectations that the European Central Bank will leave rates unchanged despite President Lagarde's warnings on energy prices. Iaccino highlights the downside momentum for the euro as the stronger U.S. economic data adds pressure across the currency complex.

items.title: Stocks slide as September CPI tops expectations.
items.excerpt: U.S. stocks trade mostly lower as hotter inflation data pushes Treasury yields higher. September CPI rose 0.6% on the month and 3.7% from a year earlier, driven by higher gasoline prices. Russell futures lead index declines, while gold, silver, copper and bitcoin also retreat against a firmer U.S. dollar. Ahead of the upcoming FOMC blackout, Fed Chair Kevin Warsh prepares to address the IMF in Bangkok. Looking ahead, market participants await quarterly earnings from regional banks and Taiwan Semiconductor, alongside U.S. retail sales, PPI and jobless claims data.

items.title: Euro futures rally from 18-month lows on dovish Fed remarks.
items.excerpt: Euro futures reversed early weakness to finish higher on Tuesday, bouncing from an 18-month low near 1.1150 to close around 1.1200. The rally was sparked by a softening U.S. dollar, following dovish remarks from New York Fed President John Williams suggesting a less aggressive stance on 2027 rate hikes. Meanwhile, FX volatility continues to ease, with the CVOL index extending its slow decline from the October 1 peak. Despite the daily bounce, fund positioning remains heavily bearish, as speculators increased their net short positions to the highest level since February 2020.
